questions.question:
Is the following statement true/false?
Access specifiers can be used for defining constructors.
questions.solution: (a) True. A constructor can be declared public, private, protected or with default access; the specifier controls where objects can be created.

questions.question: Which of the following is a return type of a constructor?
questions.solution: (d) None of the above. A constructor has no return type, not even void.

questions.question: How would the compiler/interpreter behave if there is no constructor defined in the class?

options.a: No error. Default values will be initialized to members

questions.solution: (a) No error. Default values will be initialized to members. The compiler supplies a default constructor, and instance variables get default values (0, false, null).

concepts: default value of String is null
questions.solution: (d) 0 null. No constructor sets a or c, so they keep their default values: int a = 0 and String c = null; the line prints 0, the spaces, then null.
(d) 2!. The parameterized constructor stores a = 2 and c = "!", so the values 2 and ! are printed (separated by the spaces in the string literal).

questions.question: What is the purpose of a constructor in a class?
questions.solution: (b) To initialize class data members. A constructor runs when an object is created and initializes its data members.

questions.question: What happens if no constructor is defined in a class?

options.b: A default constructor is automatically provided.
options.d: The object is created without initialization.

questions.solution: (b) A default constructor is automatically provided.. The compiler adds a default constructor, which leaves members at their default values.

questions.question: Which access specifier is most commonly used for constructors?
questions.solution: (b) Public. Constructors are usually public so that objects of the class can be created from any other class.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a parameterized constructor?
questions.solution: (c) To accept arguments for initialization. A parameterized constructor receives values as arguments and uses them to initialize the data members.

questions.topic: Creating an object with the default constructor
questions.question: Which of these correctly initializes an object using a default constructor?
questions.solution: (b) MyClass obj = new MyClass();. new MyClass() with empty brackets calls the constructor that takes no arguments; (c) only declares a reference.

questions.question: What is a formal parameter in a constructor?

options.a: A variable declared outside the constructor.
options.b: A placeholder variable declared in the constructor definition.
options.c: A variable used to call a method.
options.d: A parameter used to call another constructor.

questions.solution: (b) A placeholder variable declared in the constructor definition.. Formal parameters are declared in the constructor's heading and receive the values of the actual parameters.

questions.question: How do you define a parameterized constructor?

options.a: By providing default values to all variables.
options.b: By defining a constructor with parameters to accept values.
options.c: By using a special access specifier.
options.d: By defining a constructor without any parameters.

questions.solution: (b) By defining a constructor with parameters to accept values.. A parameterized constructor has a parameter list through which values are passed at object creation.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of constructor overloading?

options.a: A class having multiple constructors with the same name and parameter lists.
options.b: A class having multiple constructors with different parameter lists.
options.c: A class having a single constructor.
options.d: A class having private constructors only.

questions.solution: (b) A class having multiple constructors with different parameter lists.. Overloaded constructors share the class name but differ in the number, type or order of parameters.

questions.topic: Number of constructors in a class
questions.question: How many constructors can a class have?
questions.solution: A class can have any number of constructors, provided each has a different parameter list (number, type or order of parameters). This is constructor overloading.

marking_points.point: Any number of constructors, as long as their parameter lists differ

questions.topic: Why constructors have no return type
questions.question: Why do constructors not have any return type?
questions.solution: A constructor is not called to compute and return a value; it is invoked automatically by new only to initialize the object being created, and new itself gives back the reference to that object. So a constructor has no return type, not even void (its implicit return is the object of the class type).

marking_points.point: Constructor only initializes the object when it is created and is not meant to return a value (new returns the object reference / implicit return is the class type)

marking_points.point: More than one constructor in the same class with different parameter lists

questions.question: State two features of a constructor.
questions.solution:
(i) A constructor has the same name as the class.
(ii) It is invoked automatically when an object of the class is created.
(Also acceptable: it has no return type, not even void; it is used to initialize data members.)

marking_points.point: First valid feature (e.g. same name as the class)
Second valid feature (e.g. invoked automatically on object creation / no return type)

questions.question: Write the difference between default constructor and parameterized constructor.
questions.solution:
A default (non-parameterized) constructor accepts no parameters, so every object gets the same initial (default) values, e.g. Student() { marks = 0; }.
A parameterized constructor accepts arguments, so the initial values are supplied when the object is created and can differ for each object, e.g. Student(int m) { marks = m; }.

marking_points.point: Default constructor takes no parameters / gives default values
Parameterized constructor takes arguments supplied at object creation

questions.question: Can the number of actual parameters be different from the number of formal parameters?
questions.solution: No. When an object is created, the number (and types, in order) of actual parameters must match the formal parameters of the constructor being invoked; otherwise that constructor cannot be called and the compiler reports an error (unless another overloaded constructor matches the given arguments).

marking_points.point: They must match in number and type for the constructor invoked, else compile error

questions.question: If a programmer does not define a constructor in a class, can the programmer still create an object in the program?
questions.solution: Yes. If no constructor is defined, the compiler supplies a default constructor, so an object can still be created with new ClassName(); its instance variables get default values (0, 0.0, false, null).

marking_points.point: Yes, an object can be created
Because the compiler supplies a default constructor that gives default values

questions.question: State the difference between Constructor and Method.
questions.solution:
Constructor: has the same name as the class; has no return type, not even void; is invoked automatically when an object is created; is used to initialize data members.
Method: has a name different from the class name; must have a return type (void if it returns nothing); is invoked explicitly by calling it; performs some operation on the data.

marking_points.point: Automatic vs explicit invocation (or purpose: initialize vs perform a task)

questions.question:
Define a class named FruitJuice with the following description:
Instance variables/data members:
(i) int product_code – stores the product code number
(ii) String flavour – stores the flavour of the juice (e.g., orange, apple, etc.)
(iii) String pack_type – stores the type of packaging (e.g., tetra-pack, PET bottle, etc.)
(iv) int pack_size – stores the package size (e.g., 200 ml, 400 ml, etc.)
(v) int product_price – stores the price of the product
Member methods:
(i) FruitJuice() – Default constructor to initialize integer data members to 0 and String data members to "".
(ii) void input() – To input and store the product code, flavour, pack type, pack size, and product price.
(iii) void discount() – To reduce the product price by 10.
(iv) void display() – To display the product code, flavour, pack type, pack size, and product price.

marking_points.point: Class and five data members declared with correct types
Default constructor setting ints to 0 and Strings to ""
input() reading all five values with Scanner
main creates object and calls input, discount, display

questions.topic: Default and parameterized constructors: Employee salary
questions.question:
Define a Java class Employee with the following members:
Data members: code, name, basic, hra, da, PF
Default constructor: Initializes code, basic, hra, da, and PF to zero.
Parameterized constructor: Initializes basic, computes hra, da, and PF as per the following criteria:
hra = 10% of basic
da = 55% of basic
PF = Rs. 1000
Main method: Computes and displays the net salary
NetSalary = basic + da + hra – PF

marking_points.point: Class with data members code, name, basic, hra, da, PF
Default constructor initializing members to zero
Parameterized constructor computing hra = 10%, da = 55%, PF = 1000
Net salary computed as basic + da + hra - PF

questions.topic: Default constructor and rating messages: movieMagic
questions.question:
Define a class named movieMagic with the following specifications:
Instance variables/data members:
int year: To store the year of release of a movie.
String title: To store the title of the movie.
float rating: To store the popularity rating of the movie (minimum rating = 0.0 and maximum rating = 5.0).
Member methods:
(i) movieMagic(): Default constructor to initialize numeric data members to 0 and String data member to "".
(ii) void accept(): To input and store year, title, and rating.
(iii) void display(): To display the title of a movie and a message based on the rating as per the table below.
Rating | Message to be displayed
0.0 to 2.0 | Flop
2.1 to 3.4 | Semi-hit
3.5 to 4.5 | Hit
4.6 to 5.0 | Super Hit
Write a main method to create an object of the class and call the above member methods.

marking_points.point: Class and data members with correct types
accept() reading year, title and rating
if-else-if ladder for Flop / Semi-hit / Hit / Super Hit
main creates object and calls accept and display
